raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**NOTE:** We should wait to merge this one after this AITER PR makes it into a release https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6060
## Overview
Adds `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel`, an MXFP8 linear kernel for gfx950 that runs AITER's tuned FlyDSL GEMM (`gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` with 1x32 E8M0 scales). It is placed ahead of `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` (Triton `tl.dot_scaled`) in the ROCm MXFP8 kernel list. It only claims (N, K) shapes that AITER has tuned rows for; all other shapes fall through to Triton unchanged.
AITER configs: ROCm/aiter#6060 and ROCm/aiter#7411.
## Claims
- 1.2-1.9x faster per GEMM than the Triton `dot_scaled` kernel on the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP4 MXFP8 shapes at decode/verify sizes (M = 32-512). The rotating-weight micro-benchmark is below.
- In a DSpark3 conc-32 decode profile, the MXFP8 linear kernels drop from 7.46 ms to 4.28 ms per step (261 launches in both).
- No accuracy change: GSM8K is within run-to-run noise.
## Validation
**Kernel selection.** I logged the kernel chosen for every MXFP8 linear while loading MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 with TP4 and DSpark:
| Layer | N x K (per rank) | Count | Kernel |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `self_attn.qkv_proj` | 2560 x 6144 | 60 | AITER |
| `self_attn.o_proj` | 6144 x 2048 | 60 | AITER |
| `shared_experts.gate_up_proj` | 1536 x 6144 | 57 | AITER |
| `shared_experts.down_proj` | 6144 x 768 | 57 | AITER |
| dense `mlp.gate_up_proj` (main 3, draft 5) | 6144 x 6144 | 8 | AITER |
| dense `mlp.down_proj` (main 3, draft 5) | 6144 x 3072 | 8 | AITER |
| DSpark `qkv_proj` | 2304 x 6144 | 5 | AITER |
| DSpark `o_proj` | 6144 x 2048 | 5 | AITER |
| DSpark fused context K/V projection | 1280 x 6144 | 1 | AITER with ROCm/aiter#7411, Triton without it |

With `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO=1`, every layer selects `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`.

**Per-GEMM latency (µs), Triton `dot_scaled` -> AITER FlyDSL.**
- Setup: MI355X, MXFP8 weights and bf16 activations. The timing covers the full `apply_weights` path, so the activation MXFP8 quantization is included.

| N x K | M=1 | M=32 | M=128 | M=512 | M=2048 | M=8192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2560 x 6144 (QKV) | 8.5 -> 8.1 (1.04x) | 12.5 -> 8.9 (1.41x) | 23.1 -> 13.5 (1.72x) | 34.7 -> 26.8 (1.30x) | 84.9 -> 53.3 (1.59x) | 228.5 -> 173.7 (1.32x) |
| 6144 x 2048 (o_proj) | 5.8 -> 6.2 (0.94x) | 10.8 -> 6.7 (1.61x) | 11.6 -> 9.2 (1.26x) | 24.1 -> 15.5 (1.56x) | 50.7 -> 37.2 (1.36x) | 189.6 -> 127.6 (1.49x) |
| 1536 x 6144 (shared gate/up) | 8.3 -> 7.3 (1.14x) | 10.2 -> 7.8 (1.30x) | 20.0 -> 11.3 (1.76x) | 34.7 -> 20.9 (1.66x) | 46.0 -> 47.6 (0.97x) | 148.7 -> 116.9 (1.27x) |
| 6144 x 768 (shared down) | 3.9 -> 5.2 (0.76x) | 6.2 -> 5.4 (1.15x) | 7.1 -> 6.4 (1.12x) | 10.8 -> 9.8 (1.11x) | 28.8 -> 20.3 (1.42x) | 101.7 -> 61.7 (1.65x) |
| 6144 x 6144 (dense gate/up) | 13.5 -> 10.8 (1.26x) | 21.5 -> 12.5 (1.71x) | 24.4 -> 19.5 (1.25x) | 64.9 -> 36.1 (1.80x) | 132.7 -> 98.1 (1.35x) | 523.8 -> 358.4 (1.46x) |
| 6144 x 3072 (dense down) | 8.9 -> 7.4 (1.20x) | 14.0 -> 8.3 (1.68x) | 14.6 -> 12.4 (1.18x) | 35.1 -> 21.1 (1.66x) | 70.3 -> 51.6 (1.36x) | 269.6 -> 176.8 (1.52x) |
| 2304 x 6144 (DSpark QKV) | 10.0 -> 8.0 (1.24x) | 12.2 -> 8.8 (1.38x) | 23.1 -> 13.4 (1.72x) | 34.7 -> 26.1 (1.33x) | 84.2 -> 51.4 (1.64x) | 221.4 -> 160.4 (1.38x) |
| 1280 x 6144 (DSpark ctx K/V) | 9.8 -> 6.9 (1.42x) | 9.9 -> 7.5 (1.32x) | 19.0 -> 11.3 (1.69x) | 34.8 -> 18.3 (1.90x) | 44.6 -> 37.3 (1.19x) | 143.2 -> 101.7 (1.41x) |

**Decode profile.** I compared torch-profiler traces of MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (DSpark3, conc 32, TP4) with and without this kernel. The traces also contain my other MiniMax-M3 ROCm changes, which don't touch the MXFP8 linears.
| | Triton `dot_scaled` | AITER FlyDSL |
|---|---:|---:|
| MXFP8 linear time per decode step | 7.46 ms | 4.28 ms |
| MXFP8 linear launches per step | 261 | 261 |

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot strict-match, measured with the full MiniMax-M3 ROCm branch (including this kernel) against main:
| | main | with branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| conc 64, DSpark3 | 0.9621 | 0.9568 |
| conc 8, DSpark7 | 0.9591 | 0.9644 |

**e2e results**
| Conc | Metric | Nightly | Nightly + PR | Change |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | Throughput per GPU (tok/s) | 49,084 | 49,523 | +0.9% |
| 32 | ITL p50 (ms) | 6.76 | 6.53 | −3.4% |
| 32 | Interactivity p50 (tok/s/user) | 148.0 | 153.2 | +3.5% |
| 64 | Throughput per GPU (tok/s) | 57,527 | 59,563 | +3.5% |
| 64 | ITL p50 (ms) | 13.29 | 12.88 | −3.1% |
| 64 | Interactivity p50 (tok/s/user) | 75.2 | 77.6 | +3.2% |

## Details
**Opt-out:** Set `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=AiterMxfp8LinearKernel`.

nodes.body: Is this new gemm path guarded by `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` etc env?

> why we need to wait for AITER PR 7411? From that PR seems that untuned aiter gemm is still faster than vllm tl.dot kernel.

Sorry that note was supposed to link the other AITER PR https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6060, I fixed the description. The second PR ROCm/aiter#7411 is not strictly require for this one since the N=1280 layer will just fall back to Triton.

> Is this new gemm path guarded by `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` etc env?

Yep it's guarded under `rocm_aiter_ops.is_linear_enabled()` (which requires VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1) in `is_supported`.
Thanks! LGTM, let's wait for aiter v0.1.28

Thanks for this, the per-GEMM numbers look good. One compatibility question with two open MiniMax-M3.1 PRs that feed this GEMM a pre-quantized activation: #65478 (fuses the MXFP8 quant into the post-attention norm and into swiglu) and #65508 (the NVFP4 sparse decode kernel emits the MXFP8 input for `o_proj`).

Both pass a `QuantizedActivation` (row-major `[M, K/32]` E8M0 scales, `kMxfp8Dynamic`) to the linear, and only when the layer's kernel is `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`. With `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` selected first for these shapes, two things happen:

1. `apply_weights` always calls `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(x)`, so it cannot take a `QuantizedActivation`.
2. The model-side gate (`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8`) fails, so the fusions silently turn off for qkv, o_proj and the shared/dense gate_up/down in every layer. Each linear then goes back to a separate quant launch.

Could `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` accept a `QuantizedActivation` the way `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` does? Roughly:
- `input_quant_key()` returning `kMxfp8Dynamic`, and a `supports_quantized_input(layer)` that returns True when the weight is 1 byte per element.
- In `apply_weights`, `qa = as_quantized_activation(x, self.input_quant_key())`. If `qa` is not None, use `qa.data` / `qa.scale` directly, and take the output dtype and shape from `qa.orig_dtype` / `qa.orig_shape`; otherwise quantize as today.

The scale layout needs no change: the row-major E8M0 scales those fusions write are what `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` reads here (viewed as `float8_e8m0fnu`). I have this as an untested sketch and can share it if useful. On our side I'll make the model-side gate accept either kernel once the aiter kernel declares it can take quantized input, so the two PRs don't depend on landing order.

### PR Pundit review

(Testing PR Pundit Code Review agent. Not all comments may be relevant. This is a one-time automated pass: please address what is useful, no need to request a re-review. Please reply to each point, whether it applies or not: we harvest these replies, and both kinds are enormously helpful for tuning the agent. Reach out to @peymanr for suggestions.)

| # | | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🟠 | Engine startup fails with 'Failed to find a kernel' when --linear-backend=aiter and shape untuned: this PR registers a shape-gated kernel under 'aiter' | `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:364` |
| 2 | 🟠 | Model load aborts with AITER exception instead of falling back: this PR's tuned probe catches only ImportError | `vllm/_aiter_ops.py:4432` |
| 3 | 🟠 | Weight-cache daemon and IPC loader fail with UnsupportedQuantForIPCError on tuned shapes: this PR precedes RocmDotScaled without setting supports_pre_processed_weights=True | `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/aiter.py:20` |
| 4 | 🟠 | New default-first ROCm MXFP8 kernel has no selection-gating or output-parity tests | `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/aiter.py:1` |

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: Engine startup fails with 'Failed to find a kernel' when --linear-backend=aiter and shape untuned: this PR registers a shape-gated kernel under 'aiter'
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:364`

Adding `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` to `_LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP['aiter']` makes `_resolve_backend_kernels` narrow the ROCm MXFP8 list to `[AiterMxfp8LinearKernel]` whenever `--linear-backend=aiter` (or `linear_backend_per_quant={'mxfp8': 'aiter'}`) is set. Because the filtered list is non-empty, the fall-back-to-automatic-selection path no longer runs. Any MXFP8 layer this kernel rejects then makes `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` raise `ValueError('Failed to find a kernel...')` instead of using `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` or emulation. The kernel rejects a layer when its (N, K) is untuned, the default dtype is not bf16, `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO=1` is set, or `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set. The default `auto` backend is unaffected.

**Who is affected:** ROCm (gfx950) users serving MXFP8 models with `--linear-backend=aiter` or an `mxfp8: aiter` per-quant override where some layer shapes are untuned or another gate fails.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#48735](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48735) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`, [#52231](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52231) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`, [#39538](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39538) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`

#### 2. 🟠 Should fix: Model load aborts with AITER exception instead of falling back: this PR's tuned probe catches only ImportError
`vllm/_aiter_ops.py:4432`

`is_mxfp8_bpreshuffle_gemm_tuned` catches only `ImportError`, so any other error from AITER's `get_mxscale_bpreshuffle_config` escapes `can_implement` and `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` raises instead of falling through to `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`. Examples are a malformed or overridden tuned CSV (pandas/`KeyError`), an unknown arch, or an AITER with a different signature. On a supported host this is unlikely: `is_supported()` already requires a gfx95x GPU with AITER linear enabled, so `get_gfx`/`get_cu_num` succeed, and the default tuned CSV ships with AITER. The `RuntimeError` in the evidence only happens without a GPU. Catching `Exception` (or at least `(AssertionError, ImportError, KeyError, RuntimeError)`) and returning False would make the fallback robust; note the sibling `is_asm_fp4_gemm_tuned` has the same narrow catch.

**Who is affected:** ROCm gfx95x users with AITER linear enabled whose AITER install has a broken or overridden mxscale bpreshuffle tuned CSV, or a mismatched AITER version.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#46184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46184) on `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/flydsl_mxfp8_moe.py`

#### 3. 🟠 Should fix: Weight-cache daemon and IPC loader fail with UnsupportedQuantForIPCError on tuned shapes: this PR precedes RocmDotScaled without setting supports_pre_processed_weights=True
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/aiter.py:20`

`AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` leaves `supports_pre_processed_weights` at the base default `False`, while the `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` it now precedes sets it to `True`. For ModelOpt MXFP8, the quant method's `supports_pre_processed_weights` defers to the kernel's flag. As a result `check_ipc_quant_support` raises `UnsupportedQuantForIPCError` at daemon and loader startup as soon as one layer has an AITER-tuned (N, K). That error is re-raised even with fallback enabled, so the weight cache stops working where it worked before. The kernel's `process_weights_after_loading` only replaces `weight`/`weight_scale`, which the daemon exports already preshuffled, so it can most likely just declare `supports_pre_processed_weights = True`.

**Who is affected:** Users of ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoints with `--load-format ipc_cache` (weight cache daemon) on gfx950 with AITER linear enabled.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 4. 🟠 Should fix: New default-first ROCm MXFP8 kernel has no selection-gating or output-parity tests
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/aiter.py:1`

The PR adds `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` and puts it first in the ROCm MXFP8 kernel list, but no test references it. The sibling `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` has dequant-reference parity tests in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py`. Neither the new kernel's selection gating nor its output parity is tested. Untested selection gating: tuned shapes pick AITER, untuned shapes fall through to `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, and `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, non-bf16 and `bmm_batch_size` reject it. Untested output parity: `process_weights_after_loading` and `apply_weights` (shuffle layout, scale trim and E8M0 view) against a dequantized-BF16 reference. Add a CPU selection test with `is_mxfp8_bpreshuffle_gemm_tuned` monkeypatched and a gfx950 parity test.

**Who is affected:** ROCm gfx950 users serving MXFP8 checkpoints (e.g. MiniMax-M3.1) whose (N, K) shapes AITER has tuned; a regression in this path would not be caught by CI.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#15433](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/15433) on `tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py`, [#52016](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52016) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`, [#43645](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43645) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`, [#52204](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52204) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`

<sub>Shared from a pilot of [PR Pundit](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/pr_pundit), an agentic code reviewer that builds and tests the change and reads the project's past reviews. Reviewed at `69481e58`; findings checked and posted by @peymanr; points already raised on this PR are left out.</sub>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import os
+
+import torch
+
+import vllm.envs as envs
+from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+    MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE,
+    mxfp8_e4m3_quantize,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.utils import replace_parameter
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+from .Mxfp8LinearKernel import Mxfp8LinearKernel, Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig
+
+
+class AiterMxfp8LinearKernel(Mxfp8LinearKernel):
+    """MXFP8 linear on AITER's tuned FlyDSL GEMM (gfx950).
+
+    Weights are (16, 16)-preshuffled once at load; activation and weight
+    scales stay row-major E8M0, [M, K / 32] and [N, K / 32].
+    """
+
+    @classmethod
+    def is_supported(
+        cls, compute_capability: int | None = None
+    ) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
+        if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+            return False, "AITER is only supported on ROCm"
+        if not current_platform.supports_mx():
+            return False, "native MX requires CDNA4 (gfx95x)"
+        if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT:
+            return False, "tuned buckets use split K; not batch invariant"
+        if not rocm_aiter_ops.is_linear_enabled():
+            return False, "AITER linear is disabled or not supported"
+        # MiniMax-M3 mono decode re-tiles the MXFP8 QKV, output and separate
+        # shared-expert weights from the row-major layout; only the shared
+        # experts check for preshuffled weights.
+        if os.getenv("VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO", "0") in ("1", "true", "True"):
+            return False, "VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO needs row-major MXFP8 weights"
+        return True, None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def can_implement(cls, config: Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
+        N, K = config.weight_shape
+        if config.bmm_batch_size is not None:
+            return False, "batched MXFP8 GEMM is not supported"
+        # The FlyDSL GEMM writes bf16 only.
+        if torch.get_default_dtype() != torch.bfloat16:
+            return False, "requires a bf16 model"
+        if not rocm_aiter_ops.is_mxfp8_bpreshuffle_gemm_tuned(N, K):
+            return False, f"AITER has no tuned MXFP8 config for N={N}, K={K}"
+        return True, None
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight.data
+        N, K = weight.shape
+        weight_scale = layer.weight_scale.data[:N, : K // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE]
+        replace_parameter(
+            layer, "weight", rocm_aiter_ops.shuffle_weight(weight.contiguous())
+        )
+        replace_parameter(
+            layer,
+            "weight_scale",
+            weight_scale.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu),
+        )
+
+    def apply_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        out_shape = (*x.shape[:-1], layer.weight.shape[0])
+        x_q, x_scale = mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(x.reshape(-1, x.shape[-1]))
+        out = rocm_aiter_ops.gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle(
+            x_q,
+            layer.weight,
+            x_scale.view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu),
+            layer.weight_scale,
+            x.dtype,
+        )
+        out = out.reshape(out_shape)
+        if bias is not None:
+            out = out + bias
+        return out

issue_comments.body: Is this new gemm path guarded by `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` etc env?

> why we need to wait for AITER PR 7411? From that PR seems that untuned aiter gemm is still faster than vllm tl.dot kernel.

Sorry that note was supposed to link the other AITER PR https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6060, I fixed the description. The second PR ROCm/aiter#7411 is not strictly require for this one since the N=1280 layer will just fall back to Triton.

> Is this new gemm path guarded by `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` etc env?

Yep it's guarded under `rocm_aiter_ops.is_linear_enabled()` (which requires VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1) in `is_supported`.
Thanks! LGTM, let's wait for aiter v0.1.28

Thanks for this, the per-GEMM numbers look good. One compatibility question with two open MiniMax-M3.1 PRs that feed this GEMM a pre-quantized activation: #65478 (fuses the MXFP8 quant into the post-attention norm and into swiglu) and #65508 (the NVFP4 sparse decode kernel emits the MXFP8 input for `o_proj`).

Both pass a `QuantizedActivation` (row-major `[M, K/32]` E8M0 scales, `kMxfp8Dynamic`) to the linear, and only when the layer's kernel is `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`. With `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` selected first for these shapes, two things happen:

1. `apply_weights` always calls `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(x)`, so it cannot take a `QuantizedActivation`.
2. The model-side gate (`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8`) fails, so the fusions silently turn off for qkv, o_proj and the shared/dense gate_up/down in every layer. Each linear then goes back to a separate quant launch.

Could `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` accept a `QuantizedActivation` the way `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` does? Roughly:
- `input_quant_key()` returning `kMxfp8Dynamic`, and a `supports_quantized_input(layer)` that returns True when the weight is 1 byte per element.
- In `apply_weights`, `qa = as_quantized_activation(x, self.input_quant_key())`. If `qa` is not None, use `qa.data` / `qa.scale` directly, and take the output dtype and shape from `qa.orig_dtype` / `qa.orig_shape`; otherwise quantize as today.

The scale layout needs no change: the row-major E8M0 scales those fusions write are what `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` reads here (viewed as `float8_e8m0fnu`). I have this as an untested sketch and can share it if useful. On our side I'll make the model-side gate accept either kernel once the aiter kernel declares it can take quantized input, so the two PRs don't depend on landing order.

Please reply to each point, whether it applies or not: we harvest these replies, and both kinds are enormously helpful for tuning the agent. Reach out to @peymanr for suggestions.)

| # | | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🟠 | Engine startup fails with 'Failed to find a kernel' when --linear-backend=aiter and shape untuned: this PR registers a shape-gated kernel under 'aiter' | `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:364` |

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: Engine startup fails with 'Failed to find a kernel' when --linear-backend=aiter and shape untuned: this PR registers a shape-gated kernel under 'aiter'
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py:364`

Adding `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` to `_LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP['aiter']` makes `_resolve_backend_kernels` narrow the ROCm MXFP8 list to `[AiterMxfp8LinearKernel]` whenever `--linear-backend=aiter` (or `linear_backend_per_quant={'mxfp8': 'aiter'}`) is set. Because the filtered list is non-empty, the fall-back-to-automatic-selection path no longer runs. Any MXFP8 layer this kernel rejects then makes `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` raise `ValueError('Failed to find a kernel...')` instead of using `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` or emulation. The kernel rejects a layer when its (N, K) is untuned, the default dtype is not bf16, `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO=1` is set, or `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set. The default `auto` backend is unaffected.

**Who is affected:** ROCm (gfx950) users serving MXFP8 models with `--linear-backend=aiter` or an `mxfp8: aiter` per-quant override where some layer shapes are untuned or another gate fails.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#48735](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48735) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`, [#52231](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52231) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`, [#39538](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39538) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py`

#### 2. 🟠 Should fix: Model load aborts with AITER exception instead of falling back: this PR's tuned probe catches only ImportError
`vllm/_aiter_ops.py:4432`

`is_mxfp8_bpreshuffle_gemm_tuned` catches only `ImportError`, so any other error from AITER's `get_mxscale_bpreshuffle_config` escapes `can_implement` and `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` raises instead of falling through to `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`. Examples are a malformed or overridden tuned CSV (pandas/`KeyError`), an unknown arch, or an AITER with a different signature. On a supported host this is unlikely: `is_supported()` already requires a gfx95x GPU with AITER linear enabled, so `get_gfx`/`get_cu_num` succeed, and the default tuned CSV ships with AITER. The `RuntimeError` in the evidence only happens without a GPU. Catching `Exception` (or at least `(AssertionError, ImportError, KeyError, RuntimeError)`) and returning False would make the fallback robust; note the sibling `is_asm_fp4_gemm_tuned` has the same narrow catch.

**Who is affected:** ROCm gfx95x users with AITER linear enabled whose AITER install has a broken or overridden mxscale bpreshuffle tuned CSV, or a mismatched AITER version.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

**Related past reviews:** [#46184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46184) on `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/flydsl_mxfp8_moe.py`

#### 3. 🟠 Should fix: Weight-cache daemon and IPC loader fail with UnsupportedQuantForIPCError on tuned shapes: this PR precedes RocmDotScaled without setting supports_pre_processed_weights=True
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/aiter.py:20`

`AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` leaves `supports_pre_processed_weights` at the base default `False`, while the `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` it now precedes sets it to `True`. For ModelOpt MXFP8, the quant method's `supports_pre_processed_weights` defers to the kernel's flag. As a result `check_ipc_quant_support` raises `UnsupportedQuantForIPCError` at daemon and loader startup as soon as one layer has an AITER-tuned (N, K). That error is re-raised even with fallback enabled, so the weight cache stops working where it worked before. The kernel's `process_weights_after_loading` only replaces `weight`/`weight_scale`, which the daemon exports already preshuffled, so it can most likely just declare `supports_pre_processed_weights = True`.

**Who is affected:** Users of ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoints with `--load-format ipc_cache` (weight cache daemon) on gfx950 with AITER linear enabled.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._

#### 4. 🟠 Should fix: New default-first ROCm MXFP8 kernel has no selection-gating or output-parity tests
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/aiter.py:1`

The PR adds `AiterMxfp8LinearKernel` and puts it first in the ROCm MXFP8 kernel list, but no test references it. The sibling `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` has dequant-reference parity tests in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py`. Neither the new kernel's selection gating nor its output parity is tested. Untested selection gating: tuned shapes pick AITER, untuned shapes fall through to `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, and `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, non-bf16 and `bmm_batch_size` reject it. Untested output parity: `process_weights_after_loading` and `apply_weights` (shuffle layout, scale trim and E8M0 view) against a dequantized-BF16 reference. Add a CPU selection test with `is_mxfp8_bpreshuffle_gemm_tuned` monkeypatched and a gfx950 parity test.

**Who is affected:** ROCm gfx950 users serving MXFP8 checkpoints (e.g. MiniMax-M3.1) whose (N, K) shapes AITER has tuned; a regression in this path would not be caught by CI.

_Checked against the code by an independent pass._
